title: Bears safety Coby Bryant leaves first padded practice with apparent leg injury
content:
LAKE FOREST, Ill. — Safety Coby Bryant left the field in obvious discomfort Monday morning after seemingly suffering a leg injury in the Chicago Bears’ first padded practice of training camp.

The injury occurred during a period featuring safeties, tight ends and running backs. Bryant left practice and did not return. And while he was taken away from Field 4 at Halas Hall via cart, that’s not necessarily an indicator of the severity of his injury, as carts are routinely used to transport injured players from the far practice fields back to the building.

Bryant, fresh off winning a Super Bowl with the Seattle Seahawks, joined the Bears in free agency in March, signing a three-year, $40 million contract with $25.75 million guaranteed.

The Bears will now await word on Bryant’s injury and the results of any testing. Coach Ben Johnson spoke to reporters ahead of Monday’s practice and before Bryant’s exit occurred.

This story will be updated.
